The words

Onward, Christian soldiers, marching as to war,
With the cross of Jesus going on before.
Christ, the royal Master, leads against the foe;
Forward into battle see His banners go!

Refrain

Onward, Christian soldiers, marching as to war,
With the cross of Jesus going on before.

At the sign of triumph Satan’s host doth flee;
On then, Christian soldiers, on to victory!
Hell’s foundations quiver at the shout of praise;
Brothers, lift your voices, loud your anthems raise.

Like a mighty army moves the church of God;
Brothers, we are treading where the saints have trod.
We are not divided, all one body we,
One in hope and doctrine, one in charity.

Crowns and thrones may perish, kingdoms rise and wane,
But the church of Jesus constant will remain.
Gates of hell can never ’gainst that church prevail;
We have Christ’s own promise, and that cannot fail.

Onward then, ye people, join our happy throng,
Blend with ours your voices in the triumph song.
Glory, laud, and honor unto Christ the King,
This through countless ages men and angels sing.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum Eb and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on s (B♭).
  • Count the time. 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t and the chromatic fe. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

Sabine Baring-Gould wrote the words, first published in 1865. The tune, ST. GERTRUDE, is by Arthur Seymour Sullivan (1871).

  • Words (1865): Sabine Baring-Gould (1834–1924)
  • Music (1871): Arthur Seymour Sullivan (1842–1900)

Tune ST. GERTRUDE by Arthur Seymour Sullivan (1842–1900); words by Sabine Baring-Gould (1834–1924).

Questions about Onward, Christian Soldiers

What is the doh of Onward, Christian Soldiers?

In this version, in Eb major, doh is Eb. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Onward, Christian Soldiers start on?

It starts on s (B♭ in Eb major). Find doh first, then sing up or down to s.

Is Onward, Christian Soldiers in the public domain?

Yes. Sabine Baring-Gould died in 1924, Arthur Seymour Sullivan died in 1900; the words were first published in 1865 and the music in 1871. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
